bib.title: Don't Give Me the Details, Just the Summary! Topic-Aware Convolutional Neural Networks for Extreme Summarization

question: Can a one-sentence 'what is the article about' summarization task, with a dataset that does not favour extractive methods, drive abstractive modelling, and does a topic-conditioned convolutional seq2seq model do well on it?
hypothesis: Existing datasets favour extractive models; a one-sentence BBC summary dataset is less extractive, and conditioning a convolutional seq2seq model on LDA topics captures long-range and document-level content better than RNNs.
contributions: A new single-document summarization dataset (XSum) that encourages abstractive systems
Analysis and empirical results showing extractive approaches are not well suited to extreme summarization
A topic-aware convolutional sequence-to-sequence model for abstractive summarization

method.summary: XSum is built from 226,711 BBC articles whose first sentence, written by the author, is the one-line summary. T-ConvS2S extends fairseq ConvS2S with LDA word-topic and document-topic vectors in encoder and decoder. Compared against Random, LEAD, EXT-ORACLE, RNN seq2seq, pointer-generator (with and without coverage) and vanilla ConvS2S, by ROUGE, novel n-grams, best-worst human ranking and a QA test.

datasets.name: XSum
datasets.split: 90%/5%/5% random split by unique article id in the URL
datasets.source: BBC articles from Wayback archive, 2010-2017; summary is the 'story-body introduction' HTML element
datasets.preprocessing: lowercased, entities not anonymized; input truncated to 400 tokens, summary to 90 tokens; 50,000-word vocabulary

datasets.name: CNN, DailyMail, NY Times
datasets.split: CNN/DM original Hermann et al. splits; NYT Paulus et al. 2018 splits

models.name: T-ConvS2S
models.architecture: convolutional encoder-decoder with GLU, residual connections, multi-hop attention, LDA topic inputs

other.normalisation: layer normalization; weight normalization on all layers except lookup tables

models.name: Seq2Seq / PtGen / PtGen-Covg
models.architecture: RNN with attention; pointer-generator; with coverage (See et al. 2017)

models.name: Random, LEAD, EXT-ORACLE
models.architecture: extractive: random sentence, first sentence, best single sentence by ROUGE

training.objective: inferred: cross-entropy next-word prediction over the 50,000-word vocabulary (softmax output; loss not named)
training.optimizer: RNN models: Adagrad; conv models: Nesterov accelerated gradient, momentum 0.99
training.lr_schedule: conv models: once validation perplexity stopped improving, lr cut by 10x after each epoch until below 1e-4; RNN models: early stopping on validation loss
training.dropout: 0.2 on embeddings, decoder outputs and input of the convolutional blocks (conv models)
training.regularisation: RNN models: none; gradient clipping max norm 2 (RNN); conv models renormalize gradients if norm exceeds 0.1

other.gradient normalisation: by number of non-padding tokens per mini-batch
other.LDA: best of several configurations on held-out data: 512 topics

metrics.name: ROUGE-1/2/L F1
metrics.definition: pyrouge with parameters '-a -c 95 -m -n 4 -w 1.2'; R1 and R2 unigram/bigram overlap, RL longest common subsequence

metrics.name: % novel n-grams
metrics.definition: share of n-grams in the summary not present in the source document

metrics.name: Best-Worst Scaling score
metrics.definition: percent chosen best minus percent chosen worst on informativeness and fluency

metrics.name: QA score
metrics.definition: two fact questions per document answered from the summary alone; correct 1, partial 0.5, else 0; average over questions

eval.protocol: Human studies on 50 random test documents on Amazon Mechanical Turk. BWS: all pairs of 5 systems, 3 participants per comparison, one-way ANOVA with Tukey HSD, p<0.01. QA: 100 questions written from the gold summaries, 5 participants per summary. ROUGE from a single run.

limits: XSum is not diverse: a single news outlet (BBC) and a single-sentence summary style (authors' own concession).
ROUGE can mislead as the only measure of informativeness (Schluter 2017); EXT-ORACLE gets high ROUGE but low QA and human scores.
Human studies cover only 50 test documents; QA questions were written by the authors from the gold summary, which favours gold (97.23%).
No seeds, variance, parameter counts, epochs or training time reported; ROUGE gaps between T-ConvS2S variants are small (31.71 to 31.89 R1) with no significance test for them.

figures.why: Single table showing why a benchmark's extractive bias matters: LEAD R1 16.30 on XSum vs 29-40 elsewhere.
